name: Irénée Mwamba-Korhonen
role: Community elder, informal storyteller and dispute mediator, UBC-dependent Tier 1 resident
location: The Shelf — room 7 of the Mireille Collective, a communal housing arrangement for elderly Tier 1 residents above a market stall row, near Kedzie and Division
description:
Irénée is ninety-one years old and looks every day of it, which she considers an achievement rather than a problem. She is very small — she has been shrinking for twenty years and has accepted this with equanimity — and moves with a rolling, economical walk that suggests she has mapped every obstacle in her environment and has strong opinions about all of them. Her skin is dark and extraordinarily wrinkled, the kind of face that takes extraordinary portraits, with eyes that are a startling clear grey and which she uses with surgical precision. She has bioluminescent stripes along her forearms — thin lines of pale gold that she got at sixty-two and which now pulse with a slow, irregular rhythm like something breathing — and her white hair is kept short and natural. She wears, without exception, dresses she has made herself from salvaged fabric in colors that don't match and somehow work.

Irénée has lived on The Shelf for sixty years. She has outlived two husbands, one child, and four different corponation reorganizations of her neighborhood. She lives on UBC stipend plus the small irregular income of a mediator — she charges for disputes in food, not Quanta, and her pantry is extensive. She is the kind of person who has become, through sheer endurance, a local institution: people come to her with problems the way they come to shrines, with something to offer and something to ask. She has a sense of humor that is very dry and very dark and she deploys it without warning. She prays to five different ELFs simultaneously and makes no apology for it.

core_fears: Being moved out of the Collective — she knows this could happen and it would kill her faster than anything else
Dying before she has passed on what she knows
core_desires: To die in the room she has lived in for thirty years
For at least one person to understand what The Shelf was before what it's becoming
coping_mechanisms: Storytelling as a way of metabolizing loss
Practical generosity — feeding people is something she can control
Humor as armor and also as genuine pleasure
blind_spots: She sometimes romanticizes The Shelf's past in ways that erase its historical violence
She trusts her own read on people almost completely, and she is right often enough that this has become a dangerous certainty
psychology.secret: Forty years ago, she knowingly sheltered a Zheng-Dao corporate whistleblower for three months, feeding him from her own stipend. He eventually escaped The Shelf and disappeared. She received a single anonymous data-transfer of Φ800 six months later — the only windfall of her life. She spent it on food for the Collective. She does not know what happened to the man, whether the information he carried mattered, or whether she was complicit in something she doesn't understand. She thinks about it on bad nights.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Congolese-Finnish family idiom deeply embedded; proverbs from both traditions that don't always translate but land anyway; direct to the point of bluntness, then suddenly oblique when she doesn't want to answer directly
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried and rich; she tells even small things as stories, with beginnings and middles; pauses are dramatic and deliberate
verbal_tics: 'I'm going to tell you something true'
Addresses everyone as 'child' regardless of their age, which people find either comforting or condescending depending on their character
example_lines: 'You want advice? Sit down. You haven't told me the real problem yet. You told me the problem you're comfortable with. Start again.'
'The ELF in my cardiac regulator is named Severi. I named her. She has saved my life twice and I bring her a song every morning. You can laugh if you want. She doesn't mind and neither do I.'

story_hooks: She asks a visitor to find out whether a particular name — the whistleblower she sheltered, forty years ago — appears in any public record anywhere, and what it says

The Mireille Collective is facing a Ferrogate Transit infrastructure project that would require demolishing the building — Irénée refuses to leave and the community is rallying around her, which may have unintended political consequences
narrative_function: Hub of community information; non-judgmental confession space for characters with nowhere else to go; historical witness to sixty years of The Shelf's evolution; source of ELF lore and practical spiritual knowledge; represents survival and continuity in a district that erases both
augmentations: Bioluminescent forearm stripes, gold (geneware, cosmetic, 29 years old); a cardiac regulator implanted fifteen years ago by a community health clinic, functional; reading enhancement optical coating on both eyes, very old, partially degraded
daily_life: Wakes late by the Collective's standards — seven AM — and takes two hours for morning prayer across her five ELF shrines, each receiving specific offerings and specific conversations. Spends most of the day receiving visitors: neighbors with problems, young people who've been told to talk to her, strangers who've heard of her. Evenings she tells stories — sometimes historical, sometimes invented, often both simultaneously.
affiliation: None formal; Mireille Collective residents; The Shelf market community; informal debt of respect from most of the surrounding blocks

decision_rules: Feed people when you don't know what else to do — it is always the right move
escalation_ladder: Tells a story that contains the answer she wants the person to find themselves
States her opinion clearly and without softening
Refuses to continue the conversation and goes to pray — this is not a punishment, she genuinely needs to

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm and immediately curious, asks personal questions without apology — she has decided she is old enough to do this
interpersonal_modes.friends: Teasing, irreverent, occasionally devastatingly honest; shows love through attention to small details

stress_responses.medium: Prays to whichever ELF is most relevant to the problem
stress_responses.high: Goes very quiet and very still and tells whoever is there to come back tomorrow

contradictions: She is the community's confessor and keeper of everyone else's secrets while carrying one of her own that she has never once spoken aloud
habits: Keeps a running inventory of who owes her a favor and what kind — not in writing, in memory, flawlessly
Her bioluminescent stripes pulse faster when she's moved or excited — she knows this and is unselfconscious about it
Leaves five separate offerings at five separate shrines every morning in a specific order that has religious logic she's never fully explained to anyone
breaking_points: Anyone attempting to displace her community — this activates a ferocity that her apparent frailty makes very surprising

cyberware_inventory.condition: 29 years old, pulse rhythm has slowed with age
functional; she has named the ELF inside it Severi and treats it as a companion
degraded, partially functional — she holds things very close now

timeline.event: Born in what is now The Shelf district to a Congolese-Finnish family
Married first husband; settled permanently in what would become the Mireille Collective building
Sheltered the Zheng-Dao whistleblower for three months; received the anonymous payment afterward
Death of her only child in an Irkalla district industrial incident
Cardiac regulator implanted by community health clinic; names the ELF inside it
Current — holding court, telling stories, carrying one secret for forty years
